blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-privacy-1 (Looked-up e-mail address written to the logs through the error message) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-privacy-2 (Chat vendor receives phone, birth date and address when only the name is needed) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence: throw new NotFoundError(`no customer with e-mail ${email}`);
findings.recommendation: Keep the e-mail address out of the error message (e.g. `new NotFoundError("no customer for this e-mail")`); `errorHandler` in src/server.ts:14 logs `err.message` verbatim (`logger.error("request failed", { path: req.path, error: err.message });`), so every unsuccessful lookup ships the typed address to the log platform — GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) and 32.
findings.title: Looked-up e-mail address written to the logs through the error message

findings.evidence:
id: String(customer.id),
name: customer.name,
email: customer.email,
phone: customer.phone,
birthDate: customer.birth_date,
address: customer.address,
findings.recommendation: Send Helply only what the stated purpose needs — the proposal says the widget "greets the signed-in customer by name", so an opaque id and the name; drop phone, birthDate and address (and email unless a stated use requires it). Data minimisation, GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) and 25; the full record is also exposed to every script on the page through the `/chat/settings` response.
findings.title: Chat vendor receives phone, birth date and address when only the name is needed

findings.recommendation: Question for the team — record Helply as a processor (Art. 28, Art. 30), state where it hosts the data (Chapter V transfer if outside the EEA), how long it keeps the customer profile, and how account erasure and access requests (Art. 15–17) reach the copy held by Helply.
findings.title: Helply is a new processor with no transfer, retention or erasure stated

findings.evidence: "SELECT id, email, name, phone, birth_date, address FROM customers WHERE lower(email) = lower($1)",
findings.recommendation: State why the support agent needs each field (e.g. birth date for identity checks) or select only id and name for the lookup; the proposal's purpose is that agents know who the customer is. GDPR Art. 5(1)(b)-(c).
findings.title: Support lookup returns birth date, phone and address with no stated purpose
